bottleneck.description: Effective duopolist (with Murata Machinery) in semiconductor AMHS / overhead hoist transport (OHT) and FOUP-stocker systems inside 300mm/sub-3nm fabs, where vendor qualification and cleanroom integration create multi-year switching cost.

dependency.key_customers: TSMC, Samsung, Intel, Micron, SK hynix, flat-panel/OLED fabs (LG Display, Samsung Display), plus Amazon/airport/auto warehouse customers in non-cleanroom segments
dependency.key_suppliers: Motor and controls vendors (Fanuc, Yaskawa, Mitsubishi), bearings/precision mechanicals, cleanroom-grade enclosures, semiconductor controller chips

editorial.notes: Daifuku is consistently cited alongside Murata Machinery as the global leader in semiconductor AMHS (OHT segment ~46% of AMHS spend), with SEMES/SFA only meaningful inside Korea. Fab AMHS is sticky: the rail network is embedded in the cleanroom and qualified to a tool layout, so swapping vendors mid-fab is impractical. However, Daifuku's intralogistics/auto/airport segments (~50%+ of revenue) face peer competition from Dematic/KION, Honeywell, SSI Schaefer and Murata, so the bottleneck only applies to roughly half the business. That mixed profile maps to the MEDIUM tier alongside AMAT/MU rather than the HIGH-tier sole-supplier anchors.
